title: Separate successful-component counts from completed conjunctions in a finite allocation model
statement: In the specified three-candidate nine-credit synthetic Bayesian model, maximizing expected successful T+I gates and completed T-and-I lines selects different policies. The base binary64 enumeration reports approximately (3.4474 gates,0.4474 lines) versus (2.1356 gates,0.6174 lines). A hybrid bottleneck index nearly matches base completions but loses about 28.7 percent and 6.6 percent on disclosed exploratory stress cases. This is a finite-model counterexample, not an Astra effect or general allocation rule.

requires: Known iid viability q, independent fixed theory success p_t, interface success p_i conditional on latent viability, deterministic persistent preparation
Same observable histories, actions, known parameters and horizon; no hidden viability bit revealed
provides: Concrete cross-objective tradeoff and failure regions
Shared-latent repetition law q(1-(1-p_i)^k) differs from iid-marginal fiction 1-(1-q p_i)^k
Expected completed count differs from probability of any completion
assumptions: Both gates required under terminal utility; no cross-candidate transfer, theory-to-viability information or continuation value
Own-objective dominance is definitional, not an independent efficacy result
Sensitivity cases are selected, not representative or preregistered
costs: Nine charged action credits include preparation and terminal idle reservations; not nine necessarily useful calls
Planning, calibration, memory, coordination and computation uncharged; index uses exact-DP fallback
Binary64 enumeration and 12-decimal tie comparison, not exact rational arithmetic; zero success rates need separate handling
contract.units: Expected gate/line counts and action credits; no discovery, wall-time or money conversion
contract.obstruction: Shows proxy-objective risk under explicit premises. No universal interface-first rule, end-to-end cheapness, method superiority or empirical productivity.

evidence.range_scope: Original finite-horizon DP and hidden-world replay; no fresh execution claimed.
Saved binary64 base and exploratory stress outputs; no exact-rational or empirical Astra claim.

evidence.range_scope: Completed independent code audit and targeted hidden-world replay with explicit cost/failure limits.

body: Audit inspected code/results only and replayed the hard-theory case; whole sensitivity sweep was not independently rerun. Root base replay is separately reported. World-model truth remains open.
